source.text: Ἔπειτα διὰ δεκατεσσάρων ἐτῶν πάλιν ἀνέβην εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα μετὰ Βαρναβᾶ συμπαραλαβὼν καὶ Τίτον·

records.literal_gloss: Then after fourteen years again I went up to Jerusalem with Barnabas, having taken along also Titus;

en.L: Then after fourteen years I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus along also.
en.B: Then, fourteen years later, I went up to Jerusalem again, this time with Barnabas, and I took Titus along as well.
en.R: Fourteen years later I went back to Jerusalem. Barnabas went with me, and I also took Titus.

es.L: Luego, después de catorce años, subí de nuevo a Jerusalén con Bernabé, llevando también [conmigo] a Tito.
es.B: Luego, catorce años más tarde, volví a subir a Jerusalén, esta vez con Bernabé, y llevé también a Tito.
es.R: Catorce años después regresé a Jerusalén. Bernabé fue conmigo, y también llevé a Tito.

sw.L: Kisha baada ya miaka kumi na minne nilipanda tena kwenda Yerusalemu pamoja na Barnaba, nikamchukua Tito pia.
sw.B: Kisha, miaka kumi na minne baadaye, nilipanda tena Yerusalemu, safari hii pamoja na Barnaba, nikamchukua na Tito pia.
sw.R: Miaka kumi na minne baadaye nilirudi Yerusalemu. Barnaba alikwenda pamoja nami, na nilimchukua Tito pia.

decisions.choice: fourteen years counted either from Paul's call or from his first visit; the text does not say which
alternatives: fourteen years after his first visit to Jerusalem (1:18)
decisions.reason: Ἔπειτα ("then") is the word that marked each step of the story in 1:18 and 1:21, and "again" points back to the visit of 1:18. The fourteen years may be counted from that visit or from God's call in 1:15-16. Paul's point is the same either way: for years he had little contact with the Jerusalem leaders, so his gospel did not come from them.

decisions.choice: went up: the usual way of speaking of travel to Jerusalem
alternatives: a reference to rank or importance
decisions.reason: Jerusalem stands high in the hill country, and Jews spoke of going "up" to it from anywhere (1:17-18; Psalm 122:4). The word says nothing about Paul submitting to the city's leaders.

decisions.choice: Barnabas, a Jewish believer, and Titus, a Gentile believer, both Paul's fellow workers
decisions.reason: Barnabas was a Jew from Cyprus who brought Paul to the apostles and worked beside him in Antioch and on his first journey (Acts 4:36; 9:27; 11:25-26; 13:2). Titus was a Greek (verse 3) and later one of Paul's trusted helpers (2 Corinthians 8:23). Taking an uncircumcised Gentile believer to Jerusalem made him a test case, as verse 3 shows.

decisions.choice: this visit is either the famine-relief visit of Acts 11:29-30 or the meeting of Acts 15
alternatives: a visit not recorded in Acts
decisions.reason: Acts tells of Paul going to Jerusalem with Barnabas to bring help in a famine (Acts 11:29-30) and again for the meeting about circumcising Gentiles (Acts 15:1-29). Galatians 2:1-10 fits parts of both accounts. The text of Galatians does not settle which one Paul means.

decisions.choice: fourteen years later (B, R); this time with Barnabas (B); went back (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the ordinary way of saying "after fourteen years". Readable says "went back" for "went up again", since the idea of going up to Jerusalem (m2) needs no explaining at that level.

source.text: ἀνέβην δὲ κατὰ ἀποκάλυψιν· καὶ ἀνεθέμην αὐτοῖς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ὃ κηρύσσω ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, κατ’ ἰδίαν δὲ τοῖς δοκοῦσιν, μή πως εἰς κενὸν τρέχω ἢ ἔδραμον.

records.literal_gloss: I went up and according to a revelation; and I set before them the gospel which I proclaim among the Gentiles, privately but to those seeming, lest somehow in vain I run or ran.

en.L: And I went up because of a revelation, and I laid before them the gospel that I proclaim among the Gentiles, but privately, before those who seemed [to be leaders], lest somehow I might be running or had run in vain.
en.B: I went up because God had shown me that I should. I set out before them the gospel I proclaim among the Gentiles, though I did this privately, with those who were regarded as leaders. I did not want to find that I was running, or had run, for nothing.
en.R: God had shown me that I should go. I explained to them the good news I tell the Gentiles. I did it in private, with the people who were seen as leaders. I did not want all my work, past and present, to be wasted.

es.L: Y subí conforme a una revelación, y les expuse el evangelio que proclamo entre los gentiles, pero en privado, a los que parecían [ser dirigentes], no fuera que de algún modo estuviera corriendo o hubiera corrido en vano.
es.B: Subí porque Dios me había mostrado que debía hacerlo. Les presenté el evangelio que proclamo entre los gentiles, aunque lo hice en privado, ante los que eran tenidos por dirigentes. No quería descubrir que estaba corriendo, o que había corrido, en vano.
es.R: Dios me había mostrado que debía ir. Les expliqué la buena noticia que anuncio a los gentiles. Lo hice en privado, con los que eran considerados líderes. No quería que todo mi trabajo, el de antes y el de ahora, se perdiera.

sw.L: Nami nilipanda kwa sababu ya ufunuo, nikawaeleza Injili ninayoihubiri kati ya watu wa mataifa, lakini faraghani, mbele ya wale walioonekana [kuwa viongozi], nisije kwa namna fulani nikawa ninakimbia au nimekimbia bure.
sw.B: Nilipanda kwa sababu Mungu alikuwa amenionyesha kwamba nipande. Niliwaeleza Injili ninayoihubiri kati ya watu wa mataifa, ingawa nilifanya hivyo faraghani, pamoja na wale waliotambulika kuwa viongozi. Sikutaka kugundua kwamba nilikuwa ninakimbia, au nilikuwa nimekimbia, bure.
sw.R: Mungu alikuwa amenionyesha kwamba niende. Niliwaeleza Habari Njema ninayowaambia watu wa mataifa. Nilifanya hivyo faraghani, pamoja na watu waliotambulika kuwa viongozi. Sikutaka kazi yangu yote, ya zamani na ya sasa, ipotee bure.

decisions.choice: Paul went because God revealed that he should, not because the Jerusalem leaders summoned him
alternatives: he went to explain a revelation he had received
decisions.reason: ἀποκάλυψιν is the word Paul used in 1:12 for the way the gospel came to him from Jesus Christ. Here it tells why he made the journey: God directed it. The point fits his claim in chapter 1 that his gospel and his work were not handed to him by other people. The revelation may have come through a prophet, as in Acts 11:27-30, but Paul does not say.

decisions.choice: two settings: the believers in Jerusalem, and in private those regarded as leaders
alternatives: one private meeting, with the second phrase saying who "them" were
decisions.reason: αὐτοῖς ("to them") most naturally means the believers in Jerusalem, and the next phrase adds a private meeting with the leaders. It could also be one meeting, with the second phrase narrowing "them" to the leaders. Either way, Paul laid his gospel before those whose recognition mattered.

decisions.choice: those regarded as important: the recognized leaders of the Jerusalem church
alternatives: those who only seemed important but were not
decisions.reason: δοκέω means "to seem" or "to be thought", and here it names people held in high regard. Paul uses it four times in this passage (verses 2, 6 and 9), and in verse 9 he names them: James, Cephas and John. He is not mocking them; he keeps a certain distance, because their standing is not what makes the gospel true (verse 6).

decisions.choice: Paul feared his work would be undone, not that his gospel might be wrong
alternatives: Paul was unsure of his gospel and needed the leaders to confirm it
decisions.reason: Running is Paul's picture for his work, as in a race (5:7; Philippians 2:16). If the Jerusalem leaders had refused to recognize Gentile believers without circumcision, the churches he had founded would have been cut off from the believers in Judea and his work damaged. Chapter 1 rules out the thought that he doubted his gospel: he says it came by revelation (1:11-12) and curses anyone who changes it (1:8-9).

decisions.choice: because God had shown me that I should (B); God had shown me that I should go (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose revelation it was and what it was about (m1). "Revelation" alone would sound like a vision of something else.

decisions.choice: I did not want to find that I was running, or had run, for nothing (B); I did not want all my work, past and present, to be wasted (R)
alternatives: lest somehow I should be running or had run in vain
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the running picture in a separate sentence. Readable says plainly what the picture means (m4): his work now and in the past.

decisions.choice: waliotambulika kuwa viongozi
decisions.reason: "Waliohesabiwa" (those counted as) would be the obvious way to say "those who were regarded", but "kuhesabiwa" is kept for "kuhesabiwa haki" (to be justified) from verse 16 on, so "waliotambulika" (those recognized) is used for Paul's word for the leaders here and in verses 6 and 9.

source.text: ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ Τίτος ὁ σὺν ἐμοί, Ἕλλην ὤν, ἠναγκάσθη περιτμηθῆναι·

records.literal_gloss: But not even Titus the [one] with me, a Greek being, was compelled to be circumcised;

en.L: But not even Titus, who [was] with me, though he was a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised.
en.B: Yet not even Titus, who was with me, was forced to be circumcised, though he was a Greek.
en.R: Titus was with me, and he was a Greek, not a Jew. Yet even he was not forced to be circumcised.

es.L: Pero ni siquiera Tito, que [estaba] conmigo, siendo griego, fue obligado a circuncidarse.
es.B: Sin embargo, ni siquiera Tito, que estaba conmigo, fue obligado a circuncidarse, aunque era griego.
es.R: Tito estaba conmigo, y era griego, no judío. Aun así, ni siquiera a él lo obligaron a circuncidarse.

sw.L: Lakini hata Tito aliyekuwa pamoja nami, akiwa Mgiriki, hakulazimishwa kutahiriwa.
sw.B: Hata hivyo, hata Tito, aliyekuwa pamoja nami, hakulazimishwa kutahiriwa, ingawa alikuwa Mgiriki.
sw.R: Tito alikuwa pamoja nami, naye alikuwa Mgiriki, si Myahudi. Hata hivyo, hata yeye hakulazimishwa kutahiriwa.

decisions.choice: a Greek: a Gentile, someone who was not a Jew
decisions.reason: Paul often sets Ἕλλην against "Jew" to mean any Gentile (3:28; Romans 1:16). What matters here is not where Titus came from but that he was not Jewish and had not been circumcised.

decisions.choice: circumcision: the sign of God's covenant with Abraham, required of every male who joined Israel
decisions.reason: God gave circumcision to Abraham as the sign of the covenant (Genesis 17:10-14), and a Gentile man who became a Jew was circumcised. The question in Galatians is whether Gentiles who believe in Christ must also be circumcised (5:2-3; 6:12-13; Acts 15:1, 5).

decisions.choice: Titus was not circumcised: the leaders did not require it
alternatives: Titus was circumcised, but of his own free will and not under compulsion
decisions.reason: οὐδὲ ("not even") and the next verses, where Paul refuses to give way even for a moment, show that Titus stayed uncircumcised. The other reading leans on the word "compelled", but it does not fit Paul's argument: if Titus had been circumcised, the case would prove the opposite of what Paul says.

decisions.choice: he was a Greek, not a Jew
decisions.reason: Readable adds "not a Jew" to show why it mattered that Titus was a Greek (m1).

source.text: διὰ δὲ τοὺς παρεισάκτους ψευδαδέλφους, οἵτινες παρεισῆλθον κατασκοπῆσαι τὴν ἐλευθερίαν ἡμῶν ἣν ἔχομεν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, ἵνα ἡμᾶς καταδουλώσουσιν οἷς οὐδὲ πρὸς ὥραν εἴξαμεν τῇ ὑποταγῇ, ἵνα ἡ ἀλήθεια τοῦ εὐαγγελίου διαμείνῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: Because of and the secretly brought in false brothers, who slipped in to spy out the freedom of us which we have in Christ Jesus, so that us they will enslave, \v 5 to whom not even for an hour we yielded in the submission, so that the truth of the gospel might remain with you.

en.L: But because of the false brothers secretly brought in, who slipped in to spy out our freedom that we have in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus, so that they might enslave us \v 5 —to them we did not yield in submission even for an hour, so that the truth of the gospel might remain with you.
en.B: This came up because of false brothers who had been smuggled in. They slipped in to spy on the freedom we have in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, so that they could make us slaves. \v 5 We did not give in to them, not even for a moment, so that the truth of the gospel would remain with you.
en.R: The trouble came from some people who claimed to be believers but were not. They had been brought in secretly. They sneaked in to spy on the freedom we have because we belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. They wanted to make us slaves. \v 5 But we did not give in to them, not even for a moment. We wanted the truth of the good news to stay with you.

es.L: Pero a causa de los falsos hermanos introducidos a escondidas, que se infiltraron para espiar nuestra libertad que tenemos en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}, a fin de esclavizarnos \v 5 —a ellos ni por una hora cedimos en sumisión, para que la verdad del evangelio permaneciera con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Esto surgió a causa de unos falsos hermanos que habían sido introducidos a escondidas. Se infiltraron para espiar la libertad que tenemos en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}, con el fin de hacernos esclavos. \v 5 No les cedimos, ni por un momento, para que la verdad del evangelio permaneciera con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: El problema vino de algunas personas que decían ser creyentes, pero no lo eran. Las habían metido en secreto. Se colaron para espiar la libertad que tenemos porque pertenecemos {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}}. Querían hacernos esclavos. \v 5 Pero no les cedimos, ni por un momento. Queríamos que la verdad de la buena noticia se quedara con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Lakini kwa sababu ya ndugu wa uongo walioingizwa kwa siri, ambao walijipenyeza ili kupeleleza uhuru wetu tulio nao katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, ili watufanye watumwa \v 5 —kwao hatukukubali kujitiisha hata kwa saa moja, ili kweli ya Injili idumu kwenu.
sw.B: Jambo hili lilizuka kwa sababu ya ndugu wa uongo walioingizwa kwa siri. Walijipenyeza ili kupeleleza uhuru tulio nao katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, wapate kutufanya watumwa. \v 5 Hatukukubali kuwatii, hata kwa muda mfupi, ili kweli ya Injili iendelee kuwa nanyi.
sw.R: Shida ilitoka kwa watu fulani waliodai kuwa waumini, lakini hawakuwa. Walikuwa wameingizwa kwa siri. Walijipenyeza ili kupeleleza uhuru tulio nao kwa sababu sisi ni wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu. Walitaka kutufanya watumwa. \v 5 Lakini hatukukubali kuwatii, hata kwa muda mfupi. Tulitaka kweli ya Habari Njema ibaki nanyi.

decisions.choice: the sentence breaks off: the false brothers are why Titus became a test case
alternatives: "because of" goes with verse 5: because of them we did not yield
decisions.reason: Paul starts with διὰ ("because of") but never finishes the sentence; he turns to what he did about these people. The most likely link is with verse 3: the question of circumcising Titus was pressed because of them. Paul's broken grammar may show how strongly he felt about it.

decisions.choice: people who claimed to belong to the family of believers but did not, and who got in by stealth
alternatives: believers who simply disagreed with Paul
decisions.reason: ψευδάδελφος joins "false" to the word for a brother: in Paul's eyes their claim to be fellow believers was false, because they denied the gospel (1:7). παρείσακτος and παρεισέρχομαι speak of being smuggled in and slipping in, and κατασκοπέω is the word for spying. Paul presents them as infiltrators, whether at the Jerusalem meeting or earlier in Antioch (Acts 15:1).

decisions.choice: freedom in Christ from the law as a way of being accepted by God, against being made slaves under it
decisions.reason: Freedom and slavery are the poles of the whole letter (4:3-9, 4:21-5:1). To require Gentile believers to be circumcised would put them under the law as the condition of belonging to God's people, which Paul calls slavery. The freedom is had "in Christ Jesus", that is, by being joined to him.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "to whom we did not yield"
alternatives: "to whom we yielded for an hour": a few manuscripts leave out "to whom not"
decisions.reason: A few Latin witnesses and some early writers lack οἷς οὐδὲ, which would make Paul say he gave way for a short time. The great majority of Greek manuscripts have the words, and the context, where Paul insists Titus was not compelled, requires the refusal. Reviewers should check the manuscript evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the truth of the gospel: the gospel as it really is, kept for the Galatians
decisions.reason: "The truth of the gospel" (again in verse 14) is the gospel unchanged, against the distortion of 1:7. Paul resisted in Jerusalem for the sake of Gentile believers like the Galatians, so that the gospel would continue with them in its true form.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: false brothers, without a gender setting
decisions.reason: "False brothers" keeps the family word Paul uses (m2). The setting for brothers and sisters is not used here, because these are particular people pressing for circumcision at a meeting, and nothing in the text suggests a mixed group. Readable says what the phrase means: people who claimed to be believers but were not.

decisions.choice: This came up because of (B); The trouble came from (R); because we belong to (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable complete the sentence Paul leaves unfinished (m1), linking it to the question about Titus. Readable says "because we belong to" for "in Christ Jesus" (m3).

decisions.choice: con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}
decisions.reason: The chapter's only plural "you" addressed to the Galatians takes the ustedes/vosotros setting used throughout Paul's letters. In verse 14 Paul speaks to Cephas alone, with "tú".

decisions.choice: kwenu (L); nanyi (B, R)
decisions.reason: Swahili marks the plural "you" in the pronoun itself ("kwenu", "nanyi"), so the Galatians are plainly addressed without a setting.

source.text: ἀπὸ δὲ τῶν δοκούντων εἶναί τι ὁποῖοί ποτε ἦσαν οὐδέν μοι διαφέρει· πρόσωπον θεὸς ἀνθρώπου οὐ λαμβάνει ἐμοὶ γὰρ οἱ δοκοῦντες οὐδὲν προσανέθεντο, ἀλλὰ τοὐναντίον ἰδόντες ὅτι πεπίστευμαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς ἀκροβυστίας καθὼς Πέτρος τῆς περιτομῆς, ὁ γὰρ ἐνεργήσας Πέτρῳ εἰς ἀποστολὴν τῆς περιτομῆς ἐνήργησεν καὶ ἐμοὶ εἰς τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ γνόντες τὴν χάριν τὴν δοθεῖσάν μοι, Ἰάκωβος καὶ Κηφᾶς καὶ Ἰωάννης, οἱ δοκοῦντες στῦλοι εἶναι, δεξιὰς ἔδωκαν ἐμοὶ καὶ Βαρναβᾷ κοινωνίας, ἵνα ἡμεῖς εἰς τὰ ἔθνη, αὐτοὶ δὲ εἰς τὴν περιτομήν·

records.literal_gloss: From and those seeming to be something, whatever once they were nothing to me matters; face God of a man not receives; to me for those seeming nothing added, \v 7 but on the contrary having seen that I have been entrusted the gospel of the uncircumcision just as Peter of the circumcision, \v 8 for the [one] having worked in Peter for apostleship of the circumcision worked also in me for the Gentiles, \v 9 and having known the grace the [one] given to me, James and Cephas and John, those seeming pillars to be, right hands gave to me and to Barnabas of fellowship, that we to the Gentiles, they and to the circumcision;

en.L: And from those who seemed to be something (whatever they once were makes no difference to me; God does not receive [the] face of {{gender:a person|a man}}), for to me those who seemed [important] added nothing, \v 7 but on the contrary, seeing that I had been entrusted with the gospel of the uncircumcision just as Peter [had been with that] of the circumcision \v 8 (for the one who worked in Peter for [the] apostleship of the circumcision worked also in me for the Gentiles), \v 9 and knowing the grace that had been given to me, James and Cephas and John, who seemed to be pillars, gave to me and Barnabas right hands of fellowship, that we [should go] to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcision.
en.B: As for those who were regarded as important (what they once were makes no difference to me, since God is not swayed by a person's standing), those leaders added nothing to my message. \v 7 On the contrary, they saw that I had been entrusted with the gospel for the uncircumcised, just as Peter had been for the circumcised. \v 8 For God, who was at work in Peter to make him an apostle to the circumcised, was also at work in me for the Gentiles. \v 9 James, Cephas and John, who were regarded as pillars, recognized the grace that had been given to me, and they gave Barnabas and me the right hand of fellowship. We agreed that we would go to the Gentiles and they to the circumcised.
en.R: The people who were seen as leaders did not add anything to what I preach. What they once were does not matter to me. God does not favor anyone because of their position. \v 7 Instead, they saw that God had trusted me with the good news for people who are not Jews, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had trusted Peter with it for the Jews. \v 8 God was at work in Peter, making him an apostle to the Jews, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was also at work in me, sending me to the Gentiles. \v 9 James, Peter and John were seen as the pillars of the church. They recognized that God had given me this gift of grace. So they shook hands with Barnabas and me as partners. We agreed that we would go to the Gentiles, and they would go to the Jews.

es.L: Y de los que parecían ser algo (lo que hayan sido en otro tiempo nada me importa; Dios no recibe [el] rostro de {{gender:una persona|un hombre}}), pues a mí los que parecían [importantes] nada me añadieron, \v 7 sino, al contrario, viendo que se me había confiado el evangelio de la incircuncisión, así como a Pedro [el] de la circuncisión \v 8 (pues el que actuó en Pedro para [el] apostolado de la circuncisión actuó también en mí para los gentiles), \v 9 y conociendo la gracia que me había sido dada, Santiago y Cefas y Juan, que parecían ser columnas, nos dieron a mí y a Bernabé diestras de comunión, para que nosotros [fuéramos] a los gentiles, y ellos a la circuncisión.
es.B: En cuanto a los que eran tenidos por importantes (lo que hayan sido en otro tiempo no me importa, pues Dios no se deja llevar por la posición de nadie), esos dirigentes no añadieron nada a mi mensaje. \v 7 Al contrario, vieron que se me había confiado el evangelio para los incircuncisos, así como a Pedro para los circuncisos. \v 8 Porque Dios, que actuó en Pedro para hacerlo apóstol de los circuncisos, actuó también en mí para los gentiles. \v 9 Santiago, Cefas y Juan, que eran tenidos por columnas, reconocieron la gracia que se me había dado, y nos dieron a Bernabé y a mí la mano derecha de la comunión. Acordamos que nosotros iríamos a los gentiles, y ellos a los circuncisos.
es.R: Los que eran considerados líderes no añadieron nada a lo que predico. Lo que hayan sido antes no me importa. Dios no favorece a nadie por la posición que tenga. \v 7 Al contrario, vieron que Dios me había confiado la buena noticia para los que no son judíos, así como se la había confiado a Pedro para los judíos. \v 8 Dios actuaba en Pedro, haciéndolo apóstol de los judíos, y también actuaba en mí, enviándome a los gentiles. \v 9 Santiago, Pedro y Juan eran considerados las columnas de la iglesia. Reconocieron que Dios me había dado este don de gracia. Por eso nos dieron la mano a Bernabé y a mí como compañeros. Acordamos que nosotros iríamos a los gentiles, y ellos irían a los judíos.

sw.L: Lakini kutoka kwa wale walioonekana kuwa kitu (vyovyote walivyokuwa zamani, kwangu haileti tofauti; Mungu hapokei uso wa mwanadamu), kwa maana wale walioonekana [kuwa muhimu] hawakuniongezea kitu, \v 7 bali kinyume chake, walipoona kwamba nimekabidhiwa Injili ya kutotahiriwa, kama vile Petro [alivyokabidhiwa ile] ya tohara \v 8 (kwa maana aliyetenda kazi ndani ya Petro kwa ajili ya utume wa tohara alitenda kazi pia ndani yangu kwa ajili ya watu wa mataifa), \v 9 na walipoijua neema niliyopewa, Yakobo na Kefa na Yohana, walioonekana kuwa nguzo, walitupa mimi na Barnaba mikono ya kuume ya ushirika, ili sisi [twende] kwa watu wa mataifa, na wao kwa tohara.
sw.B: Kuhusu wale waliotambulika kuwa watu muhimu (walivyokuwa zamani haileti tofauti kwangu, kwa kuwa Mungu hampendelei mtu kwa sababu ya cheo chake), viongozi hao hawakuongeza chochote kwenye ujumbe wangu. \v 7 Kinyume chake, waliona kwamba nimekabidhiwa Injili kwa ajili ya wasiotahiriwa, kama vile Petro alivyokabidhiwa kwa ajili ya waliotahiriwa. \v 8 Kwa maana Mungu, aliyetenda kazi ndani ya Petro ili kumfanya mtume kwa waliotahiriwa, alitenda kazi pia ndani yangu kwa ajili ya watu wa mataifa. \v 9 Yakobo, Kefa na Yohana, waliotambulika kuwa nguzo, waliitambua neema niliyopewa, wakanipa mimi na Barnaba mkono wa kuume kama ishara ya ushirika. Tulikubaliana kwamba sisi tungeenda kwa watu wa mataifa, na wao kwa waliotahiriwa.
sw.R: Watu waliotambulika kuwa viongozi hawakuongeza chochote kwenye ujumbe ninaohubiri. Walivyokuwa zamani si muhimu kwangu. Mungu hampendelei mtu yeyote kwa sababu ya cheo chake. \v 7 Badala yake, waliona kwamba Mungu alikuwa amenikabidhi Habari Njema kwa ajili ya watu wasio Wayahudi, kama vile alivyomkabidhi Petro kwa ajili ya Wayahudi. \v 8 Mungu alitenda kazi ndani ya Petro, akamfanya mtume kwa Wayahudi, na alitenda kazi pia ndani yangu, akanituma kwa watu wa mataifa. \v 9 Yakobo, Petro na Yohana walitambulika kuwa nguzo za kanisa. Walitambua kwamba Mungu alinipa kipawa hiki cha neema. Kwa hiyo walishikana mikono nami na Barnaba kama washirika. Tulikubaliana kwamba sisi tungeenda kwa watu wa mataifa, na wao wangeenda kwa Wayahudi.

decisions.choice: the sentence breaks off and starts again: "from those who seemed" is picked up by "for to me those who seemed added nothing"
alternatives: a smooth sentence with no break
decisions.reason: Paul begins with ἀπὸ ("from"), stops to say that their standing makes no difference to him, and then begins again with ἐμοὶ γὰρ ("for to me"). The middle words are an aside. The aside and the restart both serve one point: the leaders took nothing from and added nothing to Paul's gospel.

decisions.choice: those regarded as important, the recognized leaders, here named as James, Cephas and John
decisions.reason: Paul repeats δοκέω ("those who seem") from verse 2, and in verse 9 adds "to be pillars". He accepts their standing and their agreement, but he will not treat their reputation as the measure of the gospel. The repeated word keeps that distance without mockery.

decisions.choice: whatever they once were: perhaps their having been with Jesus during his ministry
alternatives: whatever they are now, their present rank
decisions.reason: ποτε usually means "once, formerly". Paul may be thinking of what gave these men their standing, such as having known Jesus in his earthly life, or of James being the Lord's brother (1:19). It could also simply mean "whatever they were". The point is unchanged: their past or rank does not decide what the gospel is.

decisions.choice: God does not show favor according to a person's outward standing
alternatives: God does not look at people's faces
decisions.reason: To "receive the face" is a Hebrew way of saying to show partiality, to favor someone for their rank or appearance. The Law forbids it to judges and says God does not do it (Leviticus 19:15; Deuteronomy 10:17). θεὸς is the subject, and ἀνθρώπου means any human being.

decisions.choice: added nothing: required nothing more of Paul and corrected nothing in his gospel
decisions.reason: προσανατίθημι is the verb of 1:16, where Paul did not "consult" anyone. Here, with "nothing", it means the leaders laid no further demand on him, such as circumcision for his Gentile converts, and did not add anything to what he preached.

decisions.choice: entrusted with: God had given Paul the gospel to carry, as a trust
decisions.reason: πεπίστευμαι is a passive of the verb that usually means "believe". With an object it means to be entrusted with something (1 Thessalonians 2:4; 1 Timothy 1:11). The passive leaves God as the one who gave the trust, as verse 8 makes plain.

decisions.choice: one gospel taken to two peoples: the uncircumcised (Gentiles) and the circumcised (Jews)
decisions.reason: "The uncircumcision" and "the circumcision" are ways of naming Gentiles and Jews by the mark that divided them. "The gospel of" each means the gospel as taken to each people. Paul has already said there is no other gospel (1:6-7); the difference is the field of mission, not the message.

decisions.choice: the one who worked in Peter and in Paul is God
decisions.reason: ὁ ἐνεργήσας ("the one who worked") does not name the subject, but in Paul the one who works in his servants is God (1:15-16; 1 Corinthians 12:6; Philippians 2:13). The same God made Peter an apostle to the Jews and Paul to the Gentiles.

decisions.choice: James the Lord's brother; Cephas, that is, Peter; John the son of Zebedee
decisions.reason: James is the brother of the Lord mentioned in 1:19, who led the Jerusalem church (Acts 15:13; 21:18). Κηφᾶς is the Aramaic name Jesus gave Simon, meaning "rock"; Peter is the Greek form (John 1:42). Paul uses both names in these verses for the same man. John is one of the Twelve, the son of Zebedee.

decisions.choice: pillars: the main supports of God's people; right hands of fellowship: a handshake sealing a partnership
alternatives: right hands as a sign of submission
decisions.reason: A pillar holds up a building, and God's people are sometimes pictured as his house or temple (1 Corinthians 3:16; 1 Timothy 3:15). Giving the right hand was a pledge of agreement between equals. κοινωνίας is the word for sharing and partnership: the leaders recognized Paul and Barnabas as partners in the one work.

decisions.choice: an agreement about where each would work: Paul and Barnabas among Gentiles, the others among Jews
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves out the verb: "that we to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcision". The division is by people rather than by region; Paul still preached in synagogues, and Peter later ate with Gentiles in Antioch (verse 12).

decisions.choice: Cephas (L, B); Peter (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the name Paul uses here; Readable uses "Peter", the name readers know, since it is the same man (m9) and verses 7-8 already call him Peter.

decisions.choice: to my message (B, R); God (B, R in verse 8; R in verse 7); the pillars of the church (R); as partners (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the leaders added nothing to (m5) and name God as the one at work (m8). Readable says who entrusted Paul (m6), what the pillars held up and what the handshake meant (m10).

decisions.choice: receive [the] face of {{gender:a person|a man}} (L); not swayed by a person's standing (B); does not favor anyone because of their position (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the idiom, with the gender setting for a word that means any human being. Balanced and Readable say what it means (m4).

decisions.choice: the aside in verse 6 kept in brackets (B) or made separate sentences (R); verses 7-9 broken into sentences
decisions.reason: Paul's long, broken sentence becomes several English sentences. Readable puts the main point first: the leaders added nothing.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: Pronouns for God follow the reader's setting.

decisions.choice: the uncircumcised, the circumcised (B); people who are not Jews, the Jews (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of circumcision in a natural form; Readable names the two peoples (m7).

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Spanish leaves the subject pronoun inside the verb ("se la había confiado", "actuaba"), so the free "he" that carries the English setting in verses 7-8 has no Spanish counterpart, and adding "él" would sound emphatic.

decisions.choice: diestras de comunión (L); la mano derecha de la comunión (B)
alternatives: la diestra en señal de compañerismo
decisions.reason: "Comunión" is the usual Spanish word for this Greek word in Paul and keeps the link with sharing and partnership the meaning decision describes. Readable says what the handshake meant: "como compañeros".

decisions.choice: uso wa mwanadamu, no setting
decisions.reason: "Mwanadamu" is a human being, man or woman, so the English gender setting has nothing to change in Swahili, here or elsewhere in the chapter.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Swahili marks "he" inside the verb ("alivyomkabidhi", "alitenda"), and a verb prefix cannot take a capital, so the pronoun setting has no free pronoun to apply to in verses 7-8. Swahili has fewer such spans than English throughout the letter.

source.text: μόνον τῶν πτωχῶν ἵνα μνημονεύωμεν, ὃ καὶ ἐσπούδασα αὐτὸ τοῦτο ποιῆσαι.

records.literal_gloss: Only the poor that we should remember, which also I was eager this very thing to do.

en.L: Only [they asked] that we should remember the poor, the very thing that I also was eager to do.
en.B: They asked only that we keep remembering the poor, and that is the very thing I was eager to do.
en.R: They asked only one thing: that we would keep on helping the poor. That was something I was already eager to do.

es.L: Solo [pidieron] que nos acordáramos de los pobres, precisamente lo que yo también me esforcé por hacer.
es.B: Solo nos pidieron que siguiéramos acordándonos de los pobres, y eso es justamente lo que yo estaba deseoso de hacer.
es.R: Nos pidieron una sola cosa: que siguiéramos ayudando a los pobres. Eso era algo que yo ya deseaba mucho hacer.

sw.L: Ila [waliomba] tu kwamba tuwakumbuke maskini, jambo lile lile ambalo mimi pia nilijitahidi kulifanya.
sw.B: Waliomba tu kwamba tuendelee kuwakumbuka maskini, nalo ndilo jambo nililokuwa na hamu kubwa ya kulifanya.
sw.R: Waliomba jambo moja tu: kwamba tuendelee kuwasaidia maskini. Hilo nilikuwa tayari na hamu kubwa ya kulifanya.

decisions.choice: the only request the leaders added to the agreement of verse 9
alternatives: a separate request made at another time
decisions.reason: μόνον ("only") with ἵνα ("that") continues the agreement of verse 9: the one thing asked of Paul and Barnabas. It is not a condition on the gospel, which the leaders had already accepted, but a request about care for the needy.

decisions.choice: remember the poor: keep giving practical help to poor believers, especially in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: To "remember" the poor means to act for them, and the present tense says to keep doing it. Paul later gathered money from his Gentile churches "for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem" (Romans 15:26; 1 Corinthians 16:1-3). The Jerusalem believers are most likely meant, though the words could cover the poor more widely.

decisions.choice: Paul was eager to do this, and did it
alternatives: Paul became eager only after this meeting
decisions.reason: ἐσπούδασα is a past tense meaning "I was eager, I made every effort". It may look back to help he had already carried (Acts 11:29-30) or forward to the collection he later organized. Either way, Paul shows that he gladly agreed.

decisions.choice: [they asked] (L); They asked (B, R)
alternatives: Only that we should remember the poor
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves out the verb; English needs one to make a sentence (m1).

decisions.choice: keep on helping
decisions.reason: Readable says what "remember" means here (m2).

source.text: Ὅτε δὲ ἦλθεν Κηφᾶς εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν, κατὰ πρόσωπον αὐτῷ ἀντέστην, ὅτι κατεγνωσμένος ἦν·

records.literal_gloss: When but came Cephas to Antioch, to face to him I opposed, because condemned he was;

en.L: But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him to [his] face, because he stood condemned.
en.B: But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him face to face, because he was clearly in the wrong.
en.R: When Peter came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face, because he was plainly wrong.

es.L: Pero cuando Cefas vino a Antioquía, me opuse a él cara a cara, porque estaba condenado.
es.B: Pero cuando Cefas llegó a Antioquía, me enfrenté a él cara a cara, porque estaba claramente en falta.
es.R: Cuando Pedro llegó a Antioquía, me opuse a él abiertamente, cara a cara, porque era evidente que estaba equivocado.

sw.L: Lakini Kefa alipokuja Antiokia, nilimpinga uso kwa uso, kwa sababu alikuwa amehukumiwa.
sw.B: Lakini Kefa alipofika Antiokia, nilimpinga ana kwa ana, kwa sababu alikuwa amekosea waziwazi.
sw.R: Petro alipofika Antiokia, nilimpinga ana kwa ana, kwa sababu alikuwa amekosea wazi kabisa.

decisions.choice: Antioch in Syria, where Jewish and Gentile believers belonged to one church
decisions.reason: Antioch, the capital of the Roman province of Syria, had a church of Jews and Gentiles; it was the base from which Barnabas and Paul were sent out (Acts 11:19-26; 13:1-3).

decisions.choice: a new episode; whether it came after the meeting of verses 1-10 is not certain
decisions.reason: Ὅτε δὲ ("but when") turns to a new event. It most naturally follows the meeting just described, which would make Peter's conduct the more striking, but Paul may be arranging his account by subject rather than by date.

decisions.choice: he stood condemned: his own conduct showed he was in the wrong
alternatives: he had been condemned by others
decisions.reason: κατεγνωσμένος is a perfect participle of the verb "to condemn": he was in a state of being condemned. Verses 12-14 show by what: his own actions, which went against what he believed. Paul is not reporting a verdict passed by others.

decisions.choice: Cephas (L, B); Peter (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 9: Readable uses the name readers know.

decisions.choice: clearly in the wrong (B); plainly wrong (R)
decisions.reason: "Condemned" alone could suggest a court's sentence; Balanced and Readable say what Paul means (m3).

source.text: πρὸ τοῦ γὰρ ἐλθεῖν τινας ἀπὸ Ἰακώβου μετὰ τῶν ἐθνῶν συνήσθιεν· ὅτε δὲ ἦλθον, ὑπέστελλεν καὶ ἀφώριζεν ἑαυτόν, φοβούμενος τοὺς ἐκ περιτομῆς.

records.literal_gloss: Before the for to come some from James with the Gentiles he was eating; when but they came, he was drawing back and separating himself, fearing those of circumcision.

en.L: For before some [people] came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles; but when they came, he began drawing back and separating himself, fearing those of [the] circumcision.
en.B: Before some people came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles. But once they had come, he started to pull back and hold himself apart, afraid of those who insisted on circumcision.
en.R: Before some people came from James, Peter used to eat with the Gentile believers. But after they came, he began to pull away and no longer ate with them. He was afraid of the people who insisted that Gentile believers be circumcised.

es.L: Porque antes de que llegaran algunos de parte de Santiago, comía con los gentiles; pero cuando llegaron, se fue retirando y apartándose, temiendo a los de [la] circuncisión.
es.B: Antes de que llegaran algunos de parte de Santiago, solía comer con los gentiles. Pero una vez que llegaron, comenzó a retraerse y a mantenerse aparte, por miedo a los que insistían en la circuncisión.
es.R: Antes de que llegaran algunas personas de parte de Santiago, Pedro solía comer con los creyentes gentiles. Pero cuando ellos llegaron, empezó a alejarse y dejó de comer con ellos. Tenía miedo de los que insistían en que los creyentes gentiles debían circuncidarse.

sw.L: Kwa maana kabla ya kuja kwa [watu] fulani kutoka kwa Yakobo, alikuwa akila pamoja na watu wa mataifa; lakini walipokuja, akaanza kurudi nyuma na kujitenga, akiwaogopa wale wa tohara.
sw.B: Kabla watu fulani kutoka kwa Yakobo hawajafika, alikuwa na desturi ya kula pamoja na watu wa mataifa. Lakini walipofika, alianza kujiondoa na kujitenga nao, akiwaogopa wale waliosisitiza tohara.
sw.R: Kabla watu fulani kutoka kwa Yakobo hawajafika, Petro alikuwa akila pamoja na waumini wa mataifa. Lakini walipofika, alianza kujiondoa, akaacha kula pamoja nao. Aliwaogopa watu waliosisitiza kwamba waumini wa mataifa lazima watahiriwe.

decisions.choice: eating with Gentiles: sharing meals, probably including the Lord's Supper, across the line the food laws drew
decisions.reason: Many Jews avoided eating with Gentiles, because of the food laws and fear of impurity (Acts 10:28; 11:2-3). συνήσθιεν means to eat together, and in a church of Jews and Gentiles the common meal likely included the Lord's Supper (1 Corinthians 11:20-26). Peter had learned in the house of Cornelius that God accepts Gentiles (Acts 10:34-35).

decisions.choice: he used to eat with them; then he began, step by step, to draw back
alternatives: he ate once; he withdrew at once
decisions.reason: All three verbs are imperfect, the tense for something ongoing: eating with Gentiles was Peter's habit, and his withdrawal was gradual. ὑπέστελλεν can describe pulling back, as a retreating army does.

decisions.choice: people from James: from the Jerusalem church James led, perhaps sent by him
alternatives: sent by James with his authority
decisions.reason: ἀπὸ Ἰακώβου ("from James") could mean sent by James or only that they came from his circle in Jerusalem. Paul does not say that James approved of what followed.

decisions.choice: those who insisted that Gentile believers be circumcised
alternatives: Jews in general, whose pressure on the Jerusalem believers Peter feared
decisions.reason: τοὺς ἐκ περιτομῆς ("those of the circumcision") can mean Jews in general or a group within the church. Acts uses the same phrase of believers who objected to Peter eating with Gentiles (Acts 11:2), and the issue in Galatians is believers demanding circumcision (2:4; 5:2; 6:12). It could also mean unbelieving Jews whose hostility toward the Jerusalem church Peter feared.

decisions.choice: some [people] (L); some people (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the general "some"; the masculine form does not settle whether women were among them.

decisions.choice: Peter; Gentile believers; no longer ate with them
decisions.reason: Readable names Peter, says that these Gentiles were believers, and says what his separating himself meant in practice (m1).

decisions.choice: algunos
decisions.reason: Spanish "algunos" is, like the Greek word, the general "some", and can stand without a noun, so Literal needs no bracketed word where the English supplies "[people]".

source.text: καὶ συνυπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ Ἰουδαῖοι, ὥστε καὶ Βαρναβᾶς συναπήχθη αὐτῶν τῇ ὑποκρίσει.

records.literal_gloss: And acted hypocritically with him also the rest Jews, so that even Barnabas was carried away of them by the hypocrisy.

en.L: And the rest of the Jews also joined him in playing the hypocrite, so that even Barnabas was carried away by their hypocrisy.
en.B: The other Jewish believers joined in his hypocrisy, so that even Barnabas was swept along by their pretense.
en.R: The other Jewish believers in Antioch also joined Peter in this pretending. Even Barnabas was carried along by their act.

es.L: Y también los demás judíos actuaron hipócritamente junto con él, de modo que aun Bernabé fue arrastrado por la hipocresía de ellos.
es.B: Los demás creyentes judíos se unieron a su hipocresía, de modo que incluso Bernabé fue arrastrado por su simulación.
es.R: Los otros creyentes judíos de Antioquía también se unieron a Pedro en este fingimiento. Hasta Bernabé se dejó llevar por lo que ellos fingían.

sw.L: Na Wayahudi wengine nao wakaigiza unafiki pamoja naye, hata Barnaba naye akachukuliwa na unafiki wao.
sw.B: Waumini wengine wa Kiyahudi waliungana naye katika unafiki huo, hata Barnaba akachukuliwa na kujifanya kwao.
sw.R: Waumini wengine wa Kiyahudi huko Antiokia nao waliungana na Petro katika kujifanya huku. Hata Barnaba naye alivutwa na kujifanya kwao.

decisions.choice: hypocrisy: acting a part, behaving against what they believed
decisions.reason: ὑπόκρισις comes from the stage: playing a role. Peter and the others still believed that God accepted Gentile believers, yet acted as if they were unclean. Paul's charge is that their conduct contradicted their convictions, not that their faith was false.

decisions.choice: the rest of the Jews: the other Jewish believers in the Antioch church
decisions.reason: The people joining Peter in withdrawing from the shared meals are members of the church who had been eating with Gentile believers.

decisions.choice: even Barnabas: Paul's partner in the mission to the Gentiles
decisions.reason: Barnabas had gone with Paul to Jerusalem and shared in the agreement to go to the Gentiles (verses 1 and 9). καὶ ("even") marks how serious it was that he too was carried along.

decisions.choice: Jewish believers (B); Jewish believers in Antioch (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who these Jews were (m2).

decisions.choice: pretense (B); pretending, act (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "hypocrisy" once and "pretense" for the second occurrence to avoid repeating it; Readable uses plain words for acting a part (m1).

source.text: ἀλλ’ ὅτε εἶδον ὅτι οὐκ ὀρθοποδοῦσιν πρὸς τὴν ἀλήθειαν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, εἶπον τῷ Κηφᾷ ἔμπροσθεν πάντων· Εἰ σὺ Ἰουδαῖος ὑπάρχων ἐθνικῶς καὶ οὐκ Ἰουδαϊκῶς ζῇς, πῶς τὰ ἔθνη ἀναγκάζεις Ἰουδαΐζειν;

records.literal_gloss: But when I saw that not they are walking straight toward the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas before all: If you a Jew being like a Gentile and not like a Jew live, how the Gentiles do you compel to Judaize?

en.L: But when I saw that they were not walking straight according to the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of [them] all, "If you, being a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how [is it that] you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?"
en.B: But when I saw that they were not walking in step with the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of them all, "You are a Jew, yet you live like a Gentile and not like a Jew. How then can you force the Gentiles to live like Jews?"
en.R: I saw that they were not living in line with the truth of the good news. So I spoke to Peter in front of everyone. I said, "You are a Jew, but you have been living like a Gentile, not like a Jew. So how can you force Gentiles to live like Jews?"

es.L: Pero cuando vi que no andaban rectamente conforme a la verdad del evangelio, dije a Cefas delante de todos: «Si tú, siendo judío, vives como gentil y no como judío, ¿cómo obligas a los gentiles a vivir como judíos?».
es.B: Pero cuando vi que no caminaban en línea con la verdad del evangelio, dije a Cefas delante de todos: «Tú eres judío, y sin embargo vives como gentil y no como judío. ¿Cómo puedes, entonces, obligar a los gentiles a vivir como judíos?».
es.R: Vi que no estaban viviendo de acuerdo con la verdad de la buena noticia. Así que hablé con Pedro delante de todos. Le dije: «Tú eres judío, pero has estado viviendo como gentil, no como judío. Entonces, ¿cómo puedes obligar a los gentiles a vivir como judíos?».

sw.L: Lakini nilipoona kwamba hawaendi sawasawa kulingana na kweli ya Injili, nilimwambia Kefa mbele ya wote, "Ikiwa wewe, uliye Myahudi, unaishi kama mtu wa mataifa na si kama Myahudi, unawalazimishaje watu wa mataifa kuishi kama Wayahudi?"
sw.B: Lakini nilipoona kwamba mwenendo wao haupatani na kweli ya Injili, nilimwambia Kefa mbele yao wote, "Wewe ni Myahudi, lakini unaishi kama mtu wa mataifa na si kama Myahudi. Basi unawezaje kuwalazimisha watu wa mataifa kuishi kama Wayahudi?"
sw.R: Niliona kwamba hawakuwa wakiishi kulingana na kweli ya Habari Njema. Kwa hiyo nilizungumza na Petro mbele ya kila mtu. Nilimwambia, "Wewe ni Myahudi, lakini umekuwa ukiishi kama mtu wa mataifa, si kama Myahudi. Basi unawezaje kuwalazimisha watu wa mataifa kuishi kama Wayahudi?"

decisions.choice: Paul's words to Cephas are given as ending with this verse
alternatives: his words to Cephas run on to the end of the chapter (verse 21)
they run to the end of verse 15 or 16
decisions.reason: Greek has no quotation marks, so where Paul's words at Antioch end is not marked. Verses 15-16 still speak of "we" who are Jews, which fits the conversation with Cephas, but by verse 21 Paul is plainly addressing the Galatians' situation. The quotation is closed at the end of verse 14, where the direct question to Cephas ends; verses 15-21 may still continue what Paul said to him, and the meaning of those verses is the same either way.

decisions.choice: not walking straight: their conduct did not match the truth of the gospel
alternatives: not making progress toward the truth
decisions.reason: ὀρθοποδέω means to walk straight or upright. With πρὸς it means conduct in line with the gospel's truth: by separating from Gentile believers they were acting as if the gospel did not make Jews and Gentiles one (3:28).

decisions.choice: you live like a Gentile: Peter's settled way of life, free of the food laws, until his recent withdrawal
alternatives: you lived like a Gentile in the past
decisions.reason: ζῇς is present tense. Peter had made a habit of eating with Gentiles (verse 12) and was in principle still free of the food laws; his withdrawal did not change what he believed. The inconsistency is Paul's point.

decisions.choice: compel the Gentiles to live like Jews: put pressure on them, by his example, to keep the Jewish law
alternatives: to become Jewish converts by formal ceremony
decisions.reason: ἰουδαΐζω means to adopt Jewish customs, such as the food laws and circumcision. Peter gave no order, but when the leading apostle would not eat with them, Gentile believers were left with one way back to the table: to live as Jews. ἀναγκάζεις is the verb used of Titus in verse 3.

decisions.choice: Cephas (L, B); Peter (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.

decisions.choice: "You are a Jew, yet you live like a Gentile ... How then can you ...?"
alternatives: If you, being a Jew, live like a Gentile ..., how ...?
decisions.reason: The "if" states something both men knew to be true, so Balanced and Readable state it as a fact and then ask the question.

decisions.choice: tú, no plural_you setting
decisions.reason: Paul speaks to Cephas alone, with singular verbs, so Spanish uses "tú" and these words take no ustedes/vosotros setting.

source.text: Ἡμεῖς φύσει Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ οὐκ ἐξ ἐθνῶν ἁμαρτωλοί, εἰδότες δὲ ὅτι οὐ δικαιοῦται ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ἔργων νόμου ἐὰν μὴ διὰ πίστεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐπιστεύσαμεν, ἵνα δικαιωθῶμεν ἐκ πίστεως Χριστοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων νόμου, ὅτι ἐξ ἔργων νόμου οὐ δικαιωθήσεται πᾶσα σάρξ.

records.literal_gloss: We by nature Jews and not of Gentiles sinners, \v 16 knowing but that not is justified a man by works of law if not through faith of Jesus Christ, also we in Christ Jesus believed, so that we might be justified by faith of Christ and not by works of law, because by works of law not will be justified all flesh.

en.L: We [are] Jews by birth and not sinners from [the] Gentiles, \v 16 but knowing that a person is not justified by works of [the] law except through faith in Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, we also have believed in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus, so that we might be justified by faith in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} and not by works of [the] law, because by works of [the] law no flesh will be justified.
en.B: We ourselves are Jews by birth, not Gentile sinners. \v 16 Yet we know that no one is justified by works of the law; a person is justified only through faith in Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. So we too have believed in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, in order to be justified by faith in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} and not by works of the law, because no human being will be justified by works of the law.
en.R: We ourselves were born Jews. We are not Gentiles, the people Jews call sinners. \v 16 But we know that no one is put right with God by doing what the law commands. People are put right with God only through faith in Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. So we too have believed in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. We did this so that we would be put right with God by faith in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and not by doing what the law commands. For no one will be put right with God by doing what the law commands.

es.L: Nosotros [somos] judíos de nacimiento y no pecadores de entre [los] gentiles, \v 16 pero, sabiendo que una persona no es justificada por obras de [la] ley sino por medio de la fe en {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, también nosotros hemos creído en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}, para ser justificados por la fe en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} y no por obras de [la] ley, porque por obras de [la] ley ninguna carne será justificada.
es.B: Nosotros mismos somos judíos de nacimiento, no pecadores gentiles. \v 16 Pero sabemos que nadie es justificado por las obras de la ley; una persona es justificada solamente por medio de la fe en {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. Por eso también nosotros hemos creído en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}, para ser justificados por la fe en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} y no por las obras de la ley, porque ningún ser humano será justificado por las obras de la ley.
es.R: Nosotros mismos nacimos judíos. No somos gentiles, la gente a la que los judíos llaman pecadores. \v 16 Pero sabemos que Dios no declara justo a nadie por hacer lo que manda la ley. Dios declara justas a las personas solo por medio de la fe en {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. Por eso también nosotros hemos creído en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}. Lo hicimos para que Dios nos declarara justos por la fe en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, y no por hacer lo que manda la ley. Porque Dios no declarará justo a nadie por hacer lo que manda la ley.

sw.L: Sisi [ni] Wayahudi kwa kuzaliwa na si wenye dhambi kutoka [kwa] watu wa mataifa, \v 16 lakini tukijua kwamba mtu hahesabiwi haki kwa matendo ya sheria ila kwa njia ya imani katika Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, sisi nasi tumemwamini {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, ili tuhesabiwe haki kwa imani katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} na si kwa matendo ya sheria, kwa sababu kwa matendo ya sheria hakuna mwili utakaohesabiwa haki.
sw.B: Sisi wenyewe ni Wayahudi kwa kuzaliwa, si wenye dhambi wa mataifa. \v 16 Hata hivyo tunajua kwamba hakuna mtu anayehesabiwa haki kwa matendo ya sheria; mtu huhesabiwa haki kwa njia ya imani katika Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} tu. Kwa hiyo sisi pia tumemwamini {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, ili tuhesabiwe haki kwa imani katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} wala si kwa matendo ya sheria, kwa sababu hakuna binadamu atakayehesabiwa haki kwa matendo ya sheria.
sw.R: Sisi wenyewe tulizaliwa Wayahudi. Sisi si watu wa mataifa, wale ambao Wayahudi huwaita wenye dhambi. \v 16 Lakini tunajua kwamba hakuna mtu anayehesabiwa haki na Mungu kwa kutenda yale ambayo sheria inaamuru. Watu huhesabiwa haki na Mungu kwa imani katika Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} tu. Kwa hiyo sisi nasi tumemwamini {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu. Tulifanya hivyo ili tuhesabiwe haki na Mungu kwa imani katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, wala si kwa kutenda yale ambayo sheria inaamuru. Kwa maana hakuna mtu atakayehesabiwa haki na Mungu kwa kutenda yale ambayo sheria inaamuru.

decisions.choice: Gentile sinners: the Jewish way of speaking of Gentiles as outside God's law
decisions.reason: For Jews, Gentiles were "sinners" because they lived without the law God gave Israel. Paul takes up that way of speaking in order to turn it: even Jews, with all their advantages, must be justified by faith (verse 16), and in verse 17 the label falls on Jewish believers too.

decisions.choice: justified: God declares a person to be in the right before him, acquitted and accepted
alternatives: counted as a faithful member of the covenant only
decisions.reason: δικαιόω is a law-court word: to pronounce someone in the right. Paul uses it of God's verdict on a person, acquitting and accepting them (Romans 3:24-26; 8:33). Verse 17 adds that it happens "in Christ", and 2:21 and 3:6 tie it to righteousness counted to the believer.

decisions.choice: works of the law: doing what the law of Moses requires, as the ground of being accepted by God
alternatives: only the marks of Jewish identity, such as circumcision and food laws
decisions.reason: ἔργων νόμου means acts done in obedience to the law given through Moses. At Antioch the issue was food laws, and in Galatia circumcision, so those are in view; but Paul's argument goes on to the whole law (3:10-12; 5:3). His point is that keeping the law is not what puts anyone right with God.

decisions.choice: through faith in Jesus Christ
alternatives: through the faithfulness of Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: With a person's name after it, πίστις can mean faith that person has or faith directed to that person. Read the first way, Paul means Christ's own faithfulness to God, shown in his death (verse 20; Philippians 2:8), and "we have believed in Christ Jesus" is the believer's answer. Read the second way, he means the believer's faith in Christ. For "faith in Christ": the middle of the verse says just that, "we have believed in Christ Jesus", and in 3:6-9 Paul speaks of believers having faith as Abraham did. For "faithfulness of Christ": the verse would otherwise say the same thing three times, and Paul writes of "the faith of Abraham" for Abraham's own faith (Romans 4:16) and of "the faithfulness of God" (Romans 3:3). Both readings agree that justification comes from Christ and not from the law. We follow the first and give the second in a footnote.

decisions.choice: but only through faith: faith alone is the way, not faith added to works of the law
alternatives: unless also through faith, as if works and faith together justify
decisions.reason: ἐὰν μὴ normally means "except". Taken on its own it might suggest works of the law justify when joined with faith, but the rest of the verse sets faith against works three times: "by faith in Christ and not by works of the law".

decisions.choice: an echo of Psalm 143:2: no living person is righteous before God
decisions.reason: Psalm 143:2 prays that God would not enter into judgment with his servant, for no one living is righteous before him. Paul echoes the psalm and adds "by works of the law": the psalm already said that no one can stand before God on their own record. Romans 3:20 makes the same use of the psalm.

decisions.choice: all flesh: every human being
decisions.reason: πᾶσα σάρξ ("all flesh") is a common Hebrew way of saying all people, mortal and weak (Genesis 6:12; Isaiah 40:5). Here σάρξ does not carry the sense of the sinful self it has in chapter 5.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: justified (L, B); put right with God (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "justify", the word that links this verse to the rest of Paul's letters. Readable says plainly what it means (m2).

decisions.choice: works of [the] law (L); works of the law (B); doing what the law commands (R)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the article the Greek leaves out. Balanced keeps Paul's phrase, which recurs in chapter 3. Readable says what the phrase means (m3).

decisions.choice: no flesh (L); no human being (B); no one (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word "flesh". Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the Hebrew expression (m7), since "flesh" here would suggest the body or the sinful self.

decisions.choice: Gentiles, the people Jews call sinners
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that "sinners" is the Jewish label for Gentiles, not Paul's own judgment of them (m1).

decisions.choice: a person is justified only through faith
decisions.reason: Balanced states the positive side as its own clause, so that "except" is not misread (m5).

decisions.choice: justificar (L, B); Dios declara justo (R)
decisions.reason: The verb first appears in Galatians here. As in Romans, Literal and Balanced keep "justificar", so the term can be followed through the letter, and Readable says what the verdict is, "declarar justo", as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: obras de [la] ley (L); las obras de la ley (B); hacer lo que manda la ley (R); fe en
decisions.reason: Paul's phrase recurs through chapter 3, so Literal and Balanced keep "obras de la ley" every time; Readable says what it means. "Fe en" follows the reading chosen in the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: kuhesabiwa haki (all levels); na Mungu added (R)
decisions.reason: The verb first appears in Galatians here. As in Romans, "kuhesabiwa haki" (to be counted righteous) says it is a verdict and is kept at every level; Readable adds "na Mungu" to say whose verdict it is.

decisions.choice: matendo ya sheria (L, B); kutenda yale ambayo sheria inaamuru (R); imani katika
decisions.reason: "Matendo" (deeds) rather than "kazi" (work, labour), which could suggest a job. "Imani katika" (faith in) follows the reading chosen in the meaning decision; "imani ya" would leave it open but sounds like Christ's own faith.

source.text: εἰ δὲ ζητοῦντες δικαιωθῆναι ἐν Χριστῷ εὑρέθημεν καὶ αὐτοὶ ἁμαρτωλοί, ἆρα Χριστὸς ἁμαρτίας διάκονος;

records.literal_gloss: If but seeking to be justified in Christ we were found also ourselves sinners, [is] then Christ of sin a servant?

en.L: But if, while seeking to be justified in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, we ourselves also were found [to be] sinners, [is] {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} then a servant of sin?
en.B: But if, while we seek to be justified in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, we ourselves are found to be sinners too, does that make {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} a servant of sin?
en.R: We are trying to be put right with God by being joined to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Suppose this shows that we too are sinners, just like the Gentiles. Does that mean {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is working for sin?

es.L: Pero si, buscando ser justificados en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, también nosotros mismos fuimos hallados pecadores, ¿es entonces {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} servidor del pecado?
es.B: Pero si, mientras buscamos ser justificados en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, resulta que también nosotros somos pecadores, ¿hace eso {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} un servidor del pecado?
es.R: Buscamos que Dios nos declare justos por estar unidos {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}. Supongamos que esto muestra que también nosotros somos pecadores, igual que los gentiles. ¿Quiere decir eso que {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} trabaja para el pecado?

sw.L: Lakini ikiwa, tukitafuta kuhesabiwa haki katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, sisi wenyewe pia tumeonekana kuwa wenye dhambi, je, basi {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ni mtumishi wa dhambi?
sw.B: Lakini ikiwa, tunapotafuta kuhesabiwa haki katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, sisi wenyewe tunaonekana kuwa wenye dhambi pia, je, hiyo inamfanya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kuwa mtumishi wa dhambi?
sw.R: Tunatafuta kuhesabiwa haki na Mungu kwa kuunganishwa na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Tuseme jambo hili linaonyesha kwamba sisi nasi ni wenye dhambi, sawa na watu wa mataifa. Je, hiyo inamaanisha kwamba {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} anaifanyia kazi dhambi?

decisions.choice: found to be sinners: put, by leaving the law aside, in the same place as the Gentile "sinners" of verse 15
alternatives: found to be committing sins after coming to Christ
decisions.reason: Verse 15 called Gentiles "sinners" because they lived outside the law. When Jewish believers seek to be justified in Christ and not by the law, and eat with Gentiles, those who keep the law count them sinners too. Paul grants the point, in a sense: Jews also are sinners who need justifying (verse 16).

decisions.choice: a question: is Christ then a servant of sin?
alternatives: a statement: then Christ is a servant of sin
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT accents the word as ἆρα, which asks a question, and prints a question mark. The next words, "may it never be!", answer it.

decisions.choice: servant of sin: one who works for sin and promotes it
decisions.reason: διάκονος is one who serves another and acts on their behalf. The charge Paul answers is that if faith in Christ leads Jews to drop the law and be counted sinners, Christ is encouraging sin.

decisions.choice: justified in Christ: by being joined to him
alternatives: by Christ as the means only
decisions.reason: ἐν Χριστῷ is Paul's way of speaking of union with Christ: believers are justified as those who belong to him (3:26-28).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: put right with God; by being joined to; just like the Gentiles; working for sin
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain wording for "justified" set in verse 16, says what "in Christ" means (m4), links "sinners" back to verse 15 (m1), and explains "servant of sin" (m3).

decisions.choice: servidor
decisions.reason: As in Romans, "servidor" for the word for one who acts on another's behalf, keeping "siervo" and "esclavo" apart from it.

decisions.choice: mtumishi
decisions.reason: As in Romans, "mtumishi" (servant, one who acts for another) for the Greek word here; "mtumwa" is kept for a slave.

decisions.choice: the strongest possible denial
decisions.reason: μὴ γένοιτο, "may it not happen", is Paul's strongest way of rejecting a false conclusion (3:21; Romans 3:4, 6:2).

decisions.choice: Certainly not! (B); Of course not! (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use ordinary English for an emphatic no. "God forbid" adds a word for God that the Greek does not have.

decisions.choice: ¡No sea así! (L); ¡De ningún modo! (B); ¡Claro que no! (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as in Romans, so the reader meets Paul's strongest denial in one form across his letters. No word for God is added, as the English decision explains.

decisions.choice: Isiwe hivyo! (L); Hasha! (B); Sivyo kabisa! (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as in Romans, so the reader meets Paul's strongest denial in one form across his letters.

source.text: εἰ γὰρ ἃ κατέλυσα ταῦτα πάλιν οἰκοδομῶ, παραβάτην ἐμαυτὸν συνιστάνω.

records.literal_gloss: If for what I tore down these again I build, a transgressor myself I prove.

en.L: For if I build again those things that I tore down, I prove myself [to be] a transgressor.
en.B: For if I rebuild what I tore down, I show that I am a lawbreaker.
en.R: Suppose I go back to the law as the way to be right with God, after I had torn that down. Then I show that I am the one who breaks the law.

es.L: Porque si lo que derribé, eso mismo vuelvo a edificar, me muestro a mí mismo [como] transgresor.
es.B: Porque si vuelvo a edificar lo que derribé, demuestro que soy un transgresor.
es.R: Supongamos que vuelvo a la ley como el camino para estar bien con Dios, después de haberla derribado. Entonces demuestro que el que quebranta la ley soy yo.

sw.L: Kwa maana ikiwa yale niliyoyabomoa nayajenga tena, najionyesha mwenyewe [kuwa] mvunja sheria.
sw.B: Kwa maana nikijenga tena kile nilichokibomoa, ninaonyesha kwamba mimi ni mvunja sheria.
sw.R: Tuseme ninarudi kwenye sheria kama njia ya kuwa sawa mbele za Mungu, baada ya kuwa nimeibomoa. Basi ninaonyesha kwamba mimi ndiye ninayevunja sheria.

decisions.choice: what was torn down: the law as the way to be accepted by God, and the wall it set between Jews and Gentiles
decisions.reason: Building and tearing down are Paul's picture for the law's place. By eating with Gentiles, Peter had in effect torn down the food laws as a barrier (verse 12); by withdrawing, he was rebuilding it. Paul uses "I" to state the principle without naming Peter.

decisions.choice: a transgressor: one who breaks God's law
alternatives: one who disobeys a human rule
decisions.reason: παραβάτης is someone who steps over a set line. Rebuilding the law as the way to God either admits that tearing it down was wrong, or puts a person back under a law that exposes them as a lawbreaker (3:10). Either way, the sinner is not made by Christ (verse 17) but by going back to the law.

decisions.choice: go back to the law as the way to be right with God
alternatives: build again what I tore down
decisions.reason: Readable says what the building picture means (m1). It is one way of filling out the picture; the reader should know the Greek is only "what I tore down, I build again".

decisions.choice: mvunja sheria
decisions.reason: "Mkosaji" is anyone who does wrong; "mvunja sheria" (lawbreaker) keeps the picture of crossing a set line and the link with the law that the meaning decision describes.

source.text: ἐγὼ γὰρ διὰ νόμου νόμῳ ἀπέθανον ἵνα θεῷ ζήσω· Χριστῷ συνεσταύρωμαι·

records.literal_gloss: I for through law to law died so that to God I might live; with Christ I have been crucified;

en.L: For I through [the] law died to [the] law, so that I might live to God. I have been crucified with {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: For through the law I died to the law, so that I might live for God. I have been crucified with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: It was through the law that I died to the law. Now the law no longer has any claim on me, so that I can live for God. When {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} was nailed to the cross, I was nailed there with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Porque yo por medio de [la] ley morí a [la] ley, a fin de vivir para Dios. Con {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} he sido crucificado.
es.B: Porque por medio de la ley yo morí a la ley, a fin de vivir para Dios. He sido crucificado con {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}.
es.R: Fue por medio de la ley que morí a la ley. Ahora la ley ya no tiene ningún derecho sobre mí, y así puedo vivir para Dios. Cuando {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} fue clavado en la cruz, yo fui clavado allí con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

sw.L: Kwa maana mimi kwa njia ya sheria niliifia sheria, ili niishi kwa ajili ya Mungu. Pamoja na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} nimesulubiwa.
sw.B: Kwa maana kupitia sheria niliifia sheria, ili niishi kwa ajili ya Mungu. Nimesulubiwa pamoja na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Kupitia sheria yenyewe niliifia sheria. Sasa sheria haina tena mamlaka juu yangu, kwa hiyo naweza kuishi kwa ajili ya Mungu. {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alipopigiliwa misumari msalabani, mimi nilipigiliwa huko pamoja naye.

decisions.choice: "I have been crucified with Christ" ends verse 19, as the Greek verse numbers have it
decisions.reason: In the SBLGNT, as in printed Greek texts generally, Χριστῷ συνεσταύρωμαι closes verse 19. Many Bibles number the words as the start of verse 20. The words and their meaning are the same either way.

decisions.choice: the law itself brought about his death to the law: its curse fell on Christ, with whom he died
alternatives: the law showed him his sin and so drove him to Christ
decisions.reason: Paul does not explain "through the law". The next words, "crucified with Christ", and 3:13, where Christ became a curse under the law for us, suggest that the law's sentence was carried out in Christ's death, and the believer died with him. Others take it that the law, by condemning him, led him to give it up as a way to God (3:24). Both readings agree that the law itself led to this break.

decisions.choice: died to the law: the law no longer has authority over him, so that he lives for God
alternatives: he stopped caring about the law's moral teaching
decisions.reason: To die to something is to be set free from its rule (Romans 6:2, 10-11; 7:4-6). Paul does not leave the law in order to live for himself: the purpose is "that I might live for God".

decisions.choice: crucified with Christ: joined to Christ in his death, with lasting effect
decisions.reason: συνεσταύρωμαι is a perfect tense: it happened, and its effect continues. Paul shares in Christ's death because he is joined to him, as in Romans 6:6. Verse 20 draws out what follows: Christ now lives in him.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R); {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} (R)
decisions.reason: Title setting and pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: live for God
decisions.reason: "Live to God" is not natural English; "for God" gives the sense of living toward him and for his sake.

decisions.choice: the law no longer has any claim on me; nailed to the cross
decisions.reason: Readable says what dying to the law means (m3) and uses plain words for crucifixion.

decisions.choice: niliifia sheria
decisions.reason: The applied form "kufia" (to die to, die for) carries the Greek dative, so "niliifia sheria" says "I died to the law" in one verb; "nilikufa kwa sheria" could mean "I died by the law".

decisions.choice: pamoja naye, no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Swahili joins the pronoun to "na" ("naye"), the natural form, and a joined pronoun takes no capital, so the English pronoun setting on "him" has no Swahili span here.

source.text: ζῶ δὲ οὐκέτι ἐγώ, ζῇ δὲ ἐν ἐμοὶ Χριστός· ὃ δὲ νῦν ζῶ ἐν σαρκί, ἐν πίστει ζῶ τῇ τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ἀγαπήσαντός με καὶ παραδόντος ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: I live and no longer I, lives and in me Christ; what and now I live in flesh, in faith I live the of the Son of the God the [one] having loved me and having handed over himself for me.

en.L: And no longer do I live, but {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} lives in me; and what I now live in [the] flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, the one who loved me and handed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} over for me.
en.B: I am no longer the one who lives; {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} lives in me. Whatever life I still have in the flesh is a life lived by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and handed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} over for my sake.
en.R: I am no longer the one living my life. Now {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} lives in me. I still live in this human body, but I live it by faith in the Son of God. He loved me and gave up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life for me.

es.L: Y vivo, ya no yo, sino que vive en mí {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}; y lo que ahora vivo en [la] carne, en fe lo vivo, la [fe] en el Hijo de Dios, el que me amó y se entregó a {{deity_pronoun:sí mismo|Sí mismo}} por mí.
es.B: Ya no soy yo quien vive; es {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} quien vive en mí. Lo que aún me queda de vida en la carne, lo vivo por la fe en el Hijo de Dios, que me amó y se entregó a {{deity_pronoun:sí mismo|Sí mismo}} por mi bien.
es.R: Ya no soy yo quien vive mi vida. Ahora {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} vive en mí. Todavía vivo en este cuerpo humano, pero vivo por la fe en el Hijo de Dios. Él me amó y dio {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} vida por mí.

sw.L: Na ninaishi, si mimi tena, bali {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} anaishi ndani yangu; na maisha ninayoishi sasa katika mwili, ninayaishi kwa imani katika Mwana wa Mungu, yule aliyenipenda na kujitoa {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} kwa ajili yangu.
sw.B: Si mimi tena ninayeishi; {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ndiye anayeishi ndani yangu. Maisha yoyote ninayoishi bado katika mwili, ni maisha ya imani katika Mwana wa Mungu, aliyenipenda na kujitoa {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} kwa ajili yangu.
sw.R: Si mimi tena ninayeendesha maisha yangu. Sasa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} anaishi ndani yangu. Bado ninaishi katika mwili huu wa kibinadamu, lakini ninaishi kwa imani katika Mwana wa Mungu. Yeye alinipenda, akayatoa maisha {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwa ajili yangu.

decisions.choice: the old "I" died with Christ; the life Paul now lives comes from Christ living in him
decisions.reason: The "I" who lived under the law died with Christ (verse 19). Paul still lives, as the next clause says, but Christ is the source and Lord of that life. Elsewhere Paul speaks of Christ in believers by the Spirit (Romans 8:9-10).

decisions.choice: flesh: ordinary bodily, mortal human life
decisions.reason: Here σάρξ means human life in the body, as in Philippians 1:22. It is not the sinful self opposed to the Spirit that Paul speaks of in 5:13-24.

decisions.choice: by faith in the Son of God
alternatives: by the faithfulness of the Son of God
decisions.reason: As in verse 16, πίστις with a genitive can be faith directed to someone or that person's own faithfulness. The second reading points to the words that follow, "who loved me and handed himself over", as a description of the Son's own faithful act. The first fits verse 16, where "we have believed in Christ Jesus" stands between the two such phrases. We follow "faith in" and give "faithfulness of" in a footnote; both readings agree that Paul's life rests on the Son's love and death.

decisions.choice: handed himself over: gave himself up to death, for Paul's sake
decisions.reason: παραδίδωμι is the verb used of Jesus being handed over to death (Romans 4:25; 8:32). Here he hands himself over, as in 1:4, freely and out of love. "For me" makes the love personal: what Christ did for all he did for Paul.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R); {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}
decisions.reason: Title setting and pronoun setting. "Son" is God's Son and takes no setting.

decisions.choice: handed himself over
decisions.reason: "Handed over" keeps the link with the verb used of Jesus being handed over to death (m4). Readable says it plainly: he gave up his life.

decisions.choice: in this human body
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "flesh" here (m2), so that it is not read as the sinful self.

decisions.choice: I am no longer the one who lives (B); I am no longer the one living my life (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek stresses "I" at the end of the clause; Balanced and Readable bring out that emphasis: Paul lives, but not as the one in charge of his life.

decisions.choice: se entregó a {{deity_pronoun:sí mismo|Sí mismo}}
decisions.reason: The reflexive "se" is joined to the verb and takes no capital; the setting goes on the free "sí mismo".

decisions.choice: katika mwili (L, B); katika mwili huu wa kibinadamu (R)
decisions.reason: Here "flesh" is ordinary bodily life (meaning decision), so Swahili keeps "mwili" at Literal and Balanced, where it reads naturally as the body, and Readable says "mwili huu wa kibinadamu". "Asili ya dhambi" is kept for chapter 5, where the flesh is the sinful self.

source.text: οὐκ ἀθετῶ τὴν χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ· εἰ γὰρ διὰ νόμου δικαιοσύνη, ἄρα Χριστὸς δωρεὰν ἀπέθανεν.

records.literal_gloss: Not I set aside the grace of the God; if for through law righteousness, then Christ for nothing died.

en.L: I do not set aside the grace of God; for if righteousness [comes] through [the] law, then {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} died for nothing.
en.B: I do not cancel out God's grace. For if righteousness comes through the law, then {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} died for nothing at all.
en.R: I do not push God's grace aside. If people could become righteous, right with God, by keeping the law, then {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} died for no reason.

es.L: No dejo a un lado la gracia de Dios; porque si la justicia [viene] por medio de [la] ley, entonces {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} murió en vano.
es.B: No anulo la gracia de Dios. Porque si la justicia viene por medio de la ley, entonces {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} murió para nada.
es.R: Yo no hago a un lado la gracia de Dios. Si las personas pudieran llegar a ser justas, estar bien con Dios, por cumplir la ley, entonces {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} murió sin ninguna razón.

sw.L: Siiweki kando neema ya Mungu; kwa maana kama haki [huja] kupitia sheria, basi {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alikufa bure.
sw.B: Siifanyi neema ya Mungu kuwa batili. Kwa maana ikiwa haki inakuja kupitia sheria, basi {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alikufa bure kabisa.
sw.R: Mimi siisukumi kando neema ya Mungu. Kama watu wangeweza kuwa wenye haki, yaani kuwa sawa mbele za Mungu, kwa kushika sheria, basi {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alikufa bila sababu yoyote.

decisions.choice: set aside: treat as of no account, make void
decisions.reason: ἀθετέω is used of setting aside or annulling an agreement, as in 3:15. To make the law the way to righteousness would treat God's grace, shown in Christ's death, as if it counted for nothing. Paul may be answering a charge that he set aside the law; he turns it round.

decisions.choice: righteousness: a right standing before God
decisions.reason: δικαιοσύνη here goes with being justified (verses 16-17): the standing of one God declares to be in the right. Philippians 3:9 contrasts the same two sources of it, the law and faith in Christ.

decisions.choice: for nothing: without cause or purpose
decisions.reason: δωρεὰν can mean "as a gift" or "for no reason, in vain". Here only the second fits: if the law could give righteousness, Christ's death would have achieved nothing that was needed.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: people could become righteous, right with God, by keeping the law
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "righteous" and adds what it means here (m2), and says how the law would give it: by keeping it.
